differences: The shared accuracy values equal the Bark distance recomputed from the shared F1 and F2 (Traunmueller's formula, mean target of the controls of the same sex and height class) in 56 of the 80 learner-vowel sets (to 0.0025); in the other 24 sets they do not: 1 sets differ by less than 0.05 on every token, 13 sets by more (up to 9.3 Bark), and 10 have a different number of tokens in the two files. The model files therefore seem to come from another pass over the formants (or the targets) than the shared formants; that is why accuracy is shared in its own table.
The paper removed 21 outlier tokens from the 1,597 learner tokens, but the model files hold 1,537 rows (60 fewer; 34 of the missing tokens fall in the sets that match).

Table 1 of the paper does not match the deposit for several covariates: TPT_variability (paper mean 3.72, minimum 0.28; deposit 4.12, 0.93), TPT_ED (SD 0.54, minimum 0.40, maximum 3.01; deposit 0.53, 0.42, 2.99), Variability_u (mean 2.02, maximum 4.27; deposit 3.73, 29.6) and Variability_y (mean 1.64, maximum 14.96; deposit 2.49, 13.6); the paper's mean Mandarin study time is 4.37 years (SD 2.79, up to 12 years), the deposit's 4.74 (SD 3.09, up to 14).

The paper's other coefficients (variability in /u/ and /y/, beta 0.31 and 0.36) and the Wilcoxon test of /y/ against /u/ variability (V = 593) were not reproduced from the deposit's variability values (0.07 and 0.24; V = 252).
